name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+20 district lean in heavily Republican West Virginia
Incumbent Riley Moore with a large fundraising advantage
No polls or expert ratings; markets price a 97% Republican win
Challenger Ace Parsi has minimal resources
model.rationale: The district's R+20 lean, Moore's incumbency and roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge, and Polymarket pricing at 97% Republican all point to a safe Republican hold, with no evidence suggesting a competitive race.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Moore underperforming his district lean, or major outside spending against him, would be the signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's second district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about R+20. Incumbent Riley Moore is running for reelection with a commanding financial position, having raised over $1.3 million and holding more than $750,000 on hand. Democratic challenger Ace Parsi has raised roughly $134,000 with limited cash remaining, and no outside spending has materialized on either side beyond token amounts.

No public general-election polls or expert race ratings are available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets. Polymarket prices Moore's chances at about 97%. With the incumbent renominated unopposed internally and the challenger lacking resources, the race is rated Safe Republican, with only modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
